remainingIssues: npm start signal forwarding (found by the smoke runs, failed evidence ev:ev-muyqeq3m-01bde381 and ev:ev-muyqevuo-01f19e86): /bin/sh is dash, which does not exec the single command of 'sh -c node src/server.js'. When only the npm process gets SIGTERM (as some process managers do), npm signals sh, sh dies and node src/server.js is orphaned and keeps listening. Signalling the process group (terminal Ctrl-C, or kill -- -pgid) works: the server exits 0 within ~60 ms. A fix is outside this task's globs: package.json "start": "exec node src/server.js" (or running node src/server.js directly). Recommend t16 (README/package.json owner) apply it or document 'node src/server.js' for process managers.

The 2 s forced exit uses exit code 1 (spec says 'force exit after 2 s' without a code). Interpretation: a forced exit means connections were still open, so it is reported as non-zero. Not exercised by a test (would need a stalled in-flight request); the clean path (exit 0) is tested for SIGTERM and SIGINT.

In this sandbox an orphaned process lingers as a zombie until PID 1 (/process_api) reaps it, so 'kill -0' polling overstates shutdown time (~1.8 s observed). /proc state showed Z within 200 ms. Not a server issue; noted so later timing checks use /proc state, not kill -0.
